summary:
THE ABANDON BUT NOT FORGOTTEN 

Space exploration does not end when astronauts or spacecraft complete their missions. Many pieces of equipment are left behind on the Moon and Mars because they are no longer needed or cannot be brought back to Earth. Although these objects may appear abandoned, they hold important scientific and historical value.
On the Moon, NASA's Apollo missions left behind lunar lander parts, scientific instruments, tools, and Lunar Roving Vehicles. These objects provide evidence of humanity's first exploration of the lunar surface and help scientists understand the Moon.
On Mars, NASA missions such as Perseverance and InSight have also left equipment behind. Parts of Perseverance's landing system, including its parachute and backshell, remain on the Martian surface. Meanwhile, the InSight lander studied marsquakes and the planet's interior before its mission ended in 2022.
These discarded objects are more than just space debris. They are valuable reminders of human innovation, scientific discoveries, and technological achievements. Studying them helps scientists understand how missions operate, how equipment changes in space environments, and how future explorers can improve their technology.
